plan_a_advantages: Includes longer runs (14.30km - 17km) which are vital for trail running distance and endurance.
Incorporates dedicated hill sessions (60-90 minutes) to build the strength and power needed for climbing.
plan_b_advantages: Features a strength and mobility session, which can be beneficial for injury prevention and overall movement quality.
The tempo run provides a structured opportunity to work at a higher intensity, though it's less frequent than in Plan A.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates longer runs and hill sessions, which are crucial for building the specific endurance and strength required for trail running. Plan B, while including a tempo run, is significantly less demanding in terms of volume and intensity, focusing primarily on easy runs and a strength session, which doesn't directly address the speed component. Plan A’s structured approach to building both aerobic base and hill strength is more aligned with the goal of becoming a faster trail runner, while Plan B feels more geared towards general fitness.
